question.text: for a real gas at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> temperature and high pressure (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>99</mn></math> bar) the value of compressibility factor is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math>, so the value of Van 1der Waal's constant '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></math>' should be_____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>083</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> bar <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
For real gas under high pressure we can neglect pressure corrections due to intermolecular forces. But since volume will be low, we can not neglect volume corrections due to molecular size.

Z=1+PbRT = 2 ⇒b=RTP

=0.083×29899

=0.25×10-2 L mol-1
